# S76 — Derive the version from package metadata and add slicer --version

The version lives in three hand-synced places (`pyproject.toml`,
`src/slicer/__init__.py`, a README line) and there is no `slicer --version`.
Three sources drift; a release should have one.

**Findings:** v1.0.0 readiness audit (docs + code) · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** bumping the number to 1.0.0 (that is the release step),
and the PyPI name change (that is the publish slice).

## Why

A release process needs a single source of version truth and a way for users and
agents to ask the running tool its version. Hand-synced copies are a release
hazard.

## Files

- `src/slicer/__init__.py` — `__version__`
- `src/slicer/cli.py` — a top-level `--version` action
- `pyproject.toml` — remains the source of truth
- `tests/test_packaging.py`

## Failing tests

1. `slicer --version` prints the installed package version.
2. A test asserts `slicer.__version__` equals the version resolved from package
   metadata (so the two cannot drift).

## Implement

Resolve `__version__` via `importlib.metadata.version("squalor-slicer")` (fall
back cleanly when running from an uninstalled checkout), and add a top-level
`--version` flag to the argparse parser. Leave the actual bump to 1.0.0 to the
release slice; this slice makes the plumbing single-sourced.

## Check

`slicer --version` works installed and from a checkout; the drift test passes.
